stem: An adolescent boy has recurrent, unilateral, severe epistaxis; which diagnosis should be suspected?
explanation: Juvenile angiofibroma is the key diagnosis to suspect in an adolescent boy with recurrent, unilateral, severe epistaxis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because juvenile angiofibroma classically presents in adolescent males with recurrent unilateral epistaxis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because digital trauma is a common cause of epistaxis but does not specifically explain this red-flag pattern.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a blood dyscrasia can cause nosebleeds, but this presentation is more suggestive of juvenile angiofibroma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a nasal foreign body may cause epistaxis, but it is less characteristic of this adolescent male presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because winter dryness may contribute to epistaxis, but it does not account for the classic unilateral severe recurrent pattern.
